minutes.headline: Board held off certifying school enrollment for two weeks and set a special MSBA meeting; it approved a charity toll.
minutes.summary: The board approved a voluntary road toll for the boys and girls club and appointed a member to the cable access committee. The main item was the new school's enrollment number. The school building committee chair asked for a two-week extension, and the board agreed to take no vote and to meet with the MSBA at a special meeting. Members raised concerns about the size of the planned building.

decisions.decision: No official vote on enrollment certification; the board will use the two-week extension and offers of an MSBA meeting or phone conference.
A special meeting with the MSBA on enrollment will be held Tuesday August 27 as the sole agenda item, subject to confirmation by mr mackin.
The town's last submission to the MSBA will be emailed to all board members.
The board will send a letter to the Department of Public Utilities hearing on the Unitil petition.

what_happened.line: The Select Board took no vote on certifying school enrollment and will use a two-week extension requested by the school building committee chair.
A special meeting with the MSBA on enrollment is set for Tuesday August 27 as its only agenda item, subject to confirmation.
The town's last submission to the MSBA will be emailed to all board members.
The board will send a letter to the Department of Public Utilities hearing on the Unitil petition for an electric base rate increase.
The board approved a voluntary toll for the boys and girls club and appointed a member to the public access cable committee.

why_it_matters: The enrollment number the town certifies to the MSBA feeds into the size of the planned school, which affects the cost residents would be asked to carry through taxes.
The Unitil petition concerns base electric rates and a storm reserve fund, so the outcome could change electric bills for town households.
